paras: The threatened lynching of Doc Carnegie was a reported plan in late June 1888 by a mob of Black residents of Birmingham, Alabama, to take Carnegie, a Black man jailed on a charge of murdering his wife, from the jail and lynch him. Police and deputy sheriffs were put on guard at the jail, and no report of an attack or of Carnegie's fate was found. The Memphis Appeal reported the plot under the headline "Negro Lynchers Organizing," stressing that the would-be lynchers were said to be of the accused man's own race.
Carnegie, described as "the negro," was arrested and jailed on Sunday, June 24, 1888, accused of murdering his wife. The coverage does not name the wife or describe how she died.

Through June 26 and 27 it was "the talk throughout the city" that a mob of Carnegie's own race would try to lynch him. According to a Birmingham dispatch dated June 27, little credence was given to this talk until that night, when reports came in from the Black quarters on the outskirts of town that arrangements were "really under way" to march on the jail and take Carnegie at midnight. In response, the police force was placed on guard at the jail and all the deputy sheriffs were summoned.
The dispatch was sent before the planned midnight march, and no later report on whether a crowd gathered, or on any inquest, indictment or trial of Carnegie, appears in the coverage.

The only report found is a special dispatch to the Memphis Appeal, printed on its front page on June 28, 1888. Its headline, "Negro Lynchers Organizing," put the race of the rumored mob at the center of the story, while the text treated the plot as unconfirmed talk and the guard as a precaution. The dispatch offered no comment on either the accused or the would-be lynchers, and no Black-press account appears in the coverage.

accounts.label: Special dispatch from Birmingham
accounts.gist: City talk for two days held that a mob of Carnegie's own race would try to lynch him; on the night of June 27 reports from the Black quarters said a midnight march on the jail was really being arranged, and police and deputies were put on guard.

framing.detail: Headlined "Negro Lynchers Organizing," the dispatch reports the plot as rumor and the guard as precaution, without comment on the mob or the accused.
